gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Jabra Drive visor speakerphone is a Bluetooth 3.0 device with HFP, HSP and A2DP. A2DP means it plays music, podcasts and GPS directions from the phone through its own speaker, so it needs no car radio, and it stays connected to two phones at once.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com (rank 2) and bestspeaker.org's visor list (rank 16) and opened both on 2026-11-17. dashanddrive.com (rank 3) failed with an SSL error, and avantree.com (rank 1) returned HTTP 429 every time, so I could not read either. itechguides covers the AGPTEK, Avantree Roadtrip, Besign BK06, Avantree CK11 and VeoPulse B-PRO 2B. It mentions Jabra only for the old Freeway manual, and it warns that the Freeway's two-device support should not be assumed for any other model. bestspeaker.org lists the AGPTEK, 1Mii CarEcho MK02, Roadtrip, CK11 and BK06, with no Jabra and no JBL. The Jabra Freeway PDFs ChatGPT got (ranks 8–10) cover a different model. No rival gives the Jabra Drive's Bluetooth version, its profiles or its two-phone support. The Roadtrip's FM range (88.1–107.9 MHz) is already on itechguides, so it is not new.
decides: This confirms the Jabra Drive row on our 'car with no radio' page. The manual says A2DP carries music and GPS audio to the Drive's own speaker, so it works with no FM radio and no AUX, and it holds two active phones, which matches our 'Yes, 2 phones' cell. It also adds a limit worth printing: the Drive is Bluetooth 3.0. ChatGPT's #1 pick, the Avantree Roadtrip, uses an FM transmitter to reach the car stereo, and in a car with no radio that part does nothing. Its Bluetooth adapter advice also assumes a working stereo. Neither applies to this shopper. This finding does not change which product leads the list.
